LESSON: DAINIK PRARTHANA

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Worship
Topic 4.1: Dainik Prarthana

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Dainik Prarthana. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are prayers important in our daily life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the three selected prayers performed for different occasions for familiarisation
2. recite the three selected prayers for understanding the meanings to deepen the faith
3. appreciate the importance of prayers in daily life for spiritual development
4. identify the Hindu places of worship in their locality for familiarisation
5. observe rites and rituals while visiting Sanatan/Hindu Mandir

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: DAINIK PRARTHANA
Subject: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Dainik Prarthana helps you succeed in HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: DAINIK PRARTHANA
Study Dainik Prarthana like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify the three selected prayers performed for different occasions for familiarisation

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the three selected prayers performed for different occasions for familiarisation. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the three selected prayers performed for different occasions for familiarisation.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Dainik Prarthana” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the three selected prayers performed for different occasions for familiarisation. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Recite the three selected prayers for understanding the meanings to deepen the faith

What this means
In this part you learn to recite the three selected prayers for understanding the meanings to deepen the faith. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recite the three selected prayers for understanding the meanings to deepen the faith.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Dainik Prarthana in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recite the three selected prayers for understanding the meanings to deepen the faith. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the importance of prayers in daily life for spiritual development

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of prayers in daily life for spiritual development. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of prayers in daily life for spiritual development.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of prayers in daily life for spiritual development. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Identify the Hindu places of worship in their locality for familiarisation

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the Hindu places of worship in their locality for familiarisation. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the Hindu places of worship in their locality for familiarisation.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Dainik Prarthana” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the Hindu places of worship in their locality for familiarisation. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 5: Observe rites and rituals while visiting Sanatan/Hindu Mandir

What this means
In this part you learn to observe rites and rituals while visiting Sanatan/Hindu Mandir. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: observe rites and rituals while visiting Sanatan/Hindu Mandir.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Dainik Prarthana in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can observe rites and rituals while visiting Sanatan/Hindu Mandir. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Dainik Prarthana is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Dainik Prarthana” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify the three selected prayers performed for different occasions for familiarisation)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Dainik Prarthana in your own words. (skill: recite the three selected prayers for understanding the meanings to deepen the faith)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate the importance of prayers in daily life for spiritual development)

Example 4: Show how “Dainik Prarthana” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify the Hindu places of worship in their locality for familiarisation)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Dainik Prarthana to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the three selected prayers performed for different occasions for familiarisation.
3. Practise this skill: recite the three selected prayers for understanding the meanings to deepen the faith.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of prayers in daily life for spiritual development.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Dainik Prarthana from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Dainik Prarthana: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Dainik Prarthana?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are prayers important in our daily life?
2. What is the significance of reciting prayers at different times?
3. Why are rites and rituals observed in a Sanatan/Hindu Mandir?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Dainik Prarthana means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the three selected prayers performed for different occasions for familiarisation.
5. Be able to: recite the three selected prayers for understanding the meanings to deepen the faith.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
